topic: Forms of Energy and Conservation of Energy
title: Where Does Energy Go? Conservation Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A gas flame heats a pan, a bulb lights the room, a pressure cooker whistles. Heat, light and sound are three different forms of energy. When Diya turns off the stove and the warmth fades, was the energy used up, or did it go somewhere? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) we learn the forms of energy and the law of conservation of energy, for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC students, with JEE Main and NEET practice. (The forms of energy section is not in the current rationalised NCERT book, but it is in the ISC syllabus.)

A live block slides down a rough ramp while the readout tracks every joule: potential energy falls from 98 J, kinetic energy grows to 58 J and friction makes 40 J of heat, and on the graph the total stays flat at 98 J. A slow-mo replay shows friction warming both surfaces. We build the rule step by step, from the work done by friction to the total energy of an isolated system staying constant. Side by side cards compare mechanical energy and total energy, two pause-and-think questions test a bouncing ball and a ceiling fan, and Diya's kitchen shows link by link where the energy goes. Then a worked example on a falling ball, the exam trap about K = mgh, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.
